```{r setup, include=FALSE}

# Install rnaturalearthhires if not installed already
# devtools::install_github("ropensci/rnaturalearthhires")

rm(list=ls())
gc()

load.lib <- c("tidyverse", "data.table", "cowplot", "sf", 
              "zoo", "suncalc", "here", "furrr", "geosphere"
              )

install.lib <- load.lib[!load.lib %in% installed.packages()]

for(lib in install.lib) install.packages(lib,dependencies=TRUE)
sapply(load.lib,require,character=TRUE)

dir <- here(getwd())

# Since the data falls within two UTM zones and there is not an ideal projection to use, apply a custom equal area # albers projection
aea_custom <- "+proj=aea +lat_1=30 +lat_2=50 +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-124.5 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"

source(here(dir,"functions.R"))

```

!!! Note years and summary values may differ due to NOAA database updates!!!

```{r, create data directory}


survey.path <- "Data/ATM CPS Survey"

if (!dir.exists(survey.path)) {
  dir.create(survey.path, recursive = TRUE)
}

```

```{r, create data directory}


figure.path <- "Final.Figures"

if (!dir.exists(figure.path)) {
  dir.create(figure.path)
}

```

# Read data

Remember to convert length to cm to be able to use VBGF!

```{r, read.data}

full.series <- 
  fread(
    here(dir, survey.path,
         "2003.2024.ATM.Survey.with.integrated.specimen.data.csv"), 
        sep = ",") |>
  # convert mm to cm to be able to use VBGF
  mutate(standard_length = standard_length/10) |>
  distinct()

length(unique(full.series$collection))
# [1] 2006

colnames(full.series)

hist(full.series$standard_length)

sort(unique(full.series$standard_length))

```

# Spatialize the transect data 

For each haul transect, group together the starting and stopping latitudinal longitudinal coordinates and create a line string spatial object.

```{r, spatial.transects.defs}

# Create a linestring for each transect
trip_rect <- make_transect_sf(full.series, crs = 4326)

summary(trip_rect)
  
```

# Determine fishing duration

Note that for initial plots, CPUE was defined as kg/hr, but since we are estimating biomass abundance, we area is needed instead. For each haul transect, the same CPUE values are present for both computational methods.

```{r, convert.POSIXct.object}

full.series.sf <- trip_rect |>
  group_by(cruise, ship, haul, equilibrium_time.utc, collection, 
           geometry) |>
  mutate(haulback_time.pacific = 
           as.POSIXct(haulback_time.utc, 
                      tz = "America/Los_Angeles"),
         equilibrium_time.pacific = 
           as.POSIXct(equilibrium_time.utc, 
                      tz = "America/Los_Angeles")) |>
  ungroup() 

head(unique(full.series.sf$haulback_time.utc))
head(unique(full.series.sf$haulback_time.pacific))
head(unique(full.series.sf$equilibrium_time.utc))
head(unique(full.series.sf$equilibrium_time.pacific))
  
```

# Define length bin definitions for Sardine only

Because ageing is uncertain, propose length bins where the first 100 mm are grouped (considered age 0), and where every 2.25 cm is added.

```{r, length.bin.defs}

len.bins <- full.series.sf |>
  filter(scientific_name == "Sardinops sagax")

head(len.bins)

range(len.bins$standard_length)
# [1]  2.5 29.2

#------------------------------------------------------------------
# Check lowest intervals
#------------------------------------------------------------------

len_less150 <- len.bins |>
  filter(standard_length < 15.0) |>
  mutate(len.bin = "less150")

len_150to200 <- len.bins |>
  filter(standard_length >= 15.0 & standard_length < 20.0) |>
  mutate(len.bin = "150to200")

len200plus <- len.bins |>
  filter(standard_length >= 20.0) |>
  mutate(len.bin = "200+")

#------------------------------------------------------------------
# Join data sets 
#------------------------------------------------------------------

len.bins2 <- bind_rows(len_less150, len_150to200, len200plus)

```


## Extract original weight by length bin per season

```{r, raw.weight.by.length.bin.season}

# Define seasons
season.len.weight.raw <- len.bins2 |>
  filter(scientific_name == "Sardinops sagax") |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(date = date(equilibrium_time.utc)) |>
  mutate(Year = year(date),
         Season = case_when(
           month(date) %in% c(3:5) ~ "Spring",
           month(date) %in% c(6:9) ~ "Summer",
           month(date) %in% c(10:11) ~ "Fall")
  )

#-----------------------------------------
# Extract and save spring catches
#-----------------------------------------
season.weight.raw.Spring <- season.len.weight.raw |>
  filter(Season == "Spring") |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(Total_Catch_kg = sum(Species_weight), 
            .groups = "keep"
  ) |>
  ungroup()

fwrite(season.weight.raw.Spring, 
       here(dir, survey.path, 
            "season.weight.raw.Spring.csv"), 
       sep = ",")

#-----------------------------------------
# Extract and save summer catches
#-----------------------------------------
season.weight.raw.Summer <- season.len.weight.raw |>
  filter(Season == "Summer") |>
  group_by(Year, Season) |>
  summarise(Total_Catch_kg = sum(Species_weight), 
            .groups = "keep"
  ) |>
  ungroup()

fwrite(season.weight.raw.Summer, 
       here(dir, survey.path, 
            "season.weight.raw.Summer.csv"), 
       sep = ",")

```

### Test conditional weighting based on the observed length bins

```{r, Hybrid.reweight.with.real.obs.and.theoretical.2003.2025}

#---------------------------------------------------------------
# First re-weight the data using the recorded observations where 
# available, and the theoretical where not available.
#---------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Define Haul Keys
haul_keys <- c("keys")

final_hybrid_reconstruction <- len.bins2 |>
  # --- Step A: Calculate Theoretical Baseline ---
  mutate(W_theory = 7.52e-06 * standard_length^3.23) |>
  
  group_by(across(all_of(haul_keys))) |>
  mutate(
    # How much do our measured fish deviate from the 
    # 'textbook' weight?
    ## CF = (Sum of Real Weights) / (Sum of Theoretical Weights 
    ## for those same fish)
    Condition_Factor = sum(weight, na.rm = TRUE) / 
                       sum(if_else(!is.na(weight), W_theory, 0), 
                           na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # If no weights were taken at all, default the Factor to 1.0
    Condition_Factor = if_else(is.nan(Condition_Factor) | 
                                 Condition_Factor == 0, 
                               1.0, Condition_Factor),
    
    # Create a 'Best Estimate' weight for EVERY fish
    # Use real weight if we have it; use (Theory * CF) if we don't
    W_best_estimate = if_else(!is.na(weight), weight, 
                              W_theory * Condition_Factor),
    
    # Total Weight of the Subsample (now complete for all 
    # measured lengths)
    Subsample_Total_W = sum(W_best_estimate),
    Haul_Total_Catch_W = first(Species_weight)
  ) |>
  
  # --- Step B: Partition the Catch ---
  group_by(across(all_of(c(haul_keys, "len.bin")))) |>
  mutate(
    Bin_Subsample_W = sum(W_best_estimate),
    Bin_Prop = Bin_Subsample_W / first(Subsample_Total_W),
    
    # Partition the based on this hybrid proportion
    Bin_Haul_Biomass = Bin_Prop * first(Haul_Total_Catch_W),
    
    # Final 'Scaled' Individual Weight 
    # (Sum of these = Species_weight)
    Indiv_W_Scaled = Bin_Haul_Biomass / n()
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# View(final_hybrid_reconstruction)

testyears <- final_hybrid_reconstruction |> 
  filter(Month %in% c(6:9) & Year %in% c(2008,2012:2019))
range(round(testyears$Condition_Factor, 2))
# [1] 0.00 1.86

unique(is.na(len.bins2))

#---------------------------------------------------------------
# Second, define the expansion factor and summarise the output
#---------------------------------------------------------------

final_production_data <- 
  final_hybrid_reconstruction |>
  mutate(
    # 1. BIOLOGICAL WEIGHT: This is the fish's actual 
    # size (e.g., ~0.08 kg)
    ## Use this for Length-Weight plots and Condition analysis
    Bio_Weight_kg = W_best_estimate,
    
    # 2. EXPANSION WEIGHT: This is the scaled contribution (~80 kg)
    ## Use this ONLY for summing up Total Biomass or 
    ## Stacked Bar Charts
    Scaled_Biomass_Contribution = Indiv_W_Scaled,
    
    # 3. THE LINK: The 'Numerical Expansion Factor'
    ## This tells you one measured fish represents 'X' fish in 
    ## the ocean
    Expansion_Factor = 
      Scaled_Biomass_Contribution / Bio_Weight_kg
  )

# View(final_production_data)

#--------------------------------------------------------------
# Third, check the math and data quality
#--------------------------------------------------------------

# The sum of scaled weights should exactly match
# the recorded total species weight
sum(final_production_data$Scaled_Biomass_Contribution) - sum(unique(final_production_data$Species_weight))
# [1] 379.657

#-----------------------------

# The scaled biomass is not capturing the observed
# weights well. Check if the issue lies in the fish weight 
# data wrangling step
error_report <- final_production_data |>
  group_by(across(all_of(haul_keys))) |>
  summarise(
    Expected = first(Species_weight),
    Actual = sum(Indiv_W_Scaled),
    Diff = Expected - Actual
  ) |>
  filter(abs(Diff) > 0.001)

# View(error_report)

#-----------------------------

# It seems the math is correct and the issue
# is likely in the sample size relative to the
# Haul size. Check if the subsample size (being far smaller) is 
# not representative of the haul
summary(final_production_data$Expansion_Factor)

# That Max of 2.367e+04 (23,670x) means that for at least one haul, a single measured fish (or a tiny gram-sized subsample) is being used to represent over 23 tons of catch.

# While the math is correct, the uncertainty in those specific rows is massive. If that one fish happened to be an outlier, it’s now a 23-ton outlier.

# What the Summary tells us:

# Min (0.48): Some "subsamples" were actually heavier than the recorded species weight (likely a data entry error or a "dirty" weight including debris), effectively scaling the fish down.

# Median (2.82): This is very healthy. It means for half your data, you measured about 1/3rd of the total catch. That’s high-quality sampling.

# Mean (69.47): The mean is being pulled way up by those massive outliers (the Max).

#-----------------------------

# See if the culprit year is 2007, 
# this was an issue earlier too
final_production_data.minus.2007 <- 
  final_production_data |>
  filter(Year != 2007)

summary(final_production_data.minus.2007$Expansion_Factor)

# What the Summary tells us:

# The Median (2.89) and 3rd Quartile (12.08) are excellent. This tells us that for 75% of your data, the expansion factor is 12 or less. This is highly reliable sampling.

# The Lower Bound (0.48): This still suggests some "over-sampling" where the measured basket was recorded as heavier than the total catch. This often happens if the "Total Weight" was an estimate by the captain while the "Subsample" was weighed on a high-precision scale.

# The Upper Tail (1,292): You now only have a few "stretch" hauls rather than a dataset dominated by an extreme year.

#-----------------------------

# Check if expansion factors larger than 500 are common
biomass_audit.minus.2007 <- 
  final_production_data.minus.2007 |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(Expansion_Bin = 
           cut(Expansion_Factor,
               breaks = c(0, 10, 100, 1000, Inf),
               labels = c("1-10 (High)", 
                          "10-100 (Med)", 
                          "100-1000 (Low)", 
                          ">1000 (Extreme)"))) |>
  group_by(Expansion_Bin) |>
  summarise(
    Record_Count = n(),
    Total_Biomass_Represented = 
      sum(Scaled_Biomass_Contribution)
  ) |>
  mutate(Percent_of_Total_Biomass = 
           Total_Biomass_Represented / 
           sum(Total_Biomass_Represented) * 100)

# View(biomass_audit.minus.2007)

fwrite(biomass_audit.minus.2007,
       here(dir, survey.path,
            "CPS.ATM.Survey.Biomass.audit.minus.2007.csv"), 
       sep = ",")

top_influence_hauls <- 
  final_production_data.minus.2007 |>
  filter(Expansion_Factor > 100) |>
  group_by(keys, cruise, ship, haul, collection,
           equilibrium_time.utc) |>
  summarise(
    Total_Weight_kg = first(Species_weight),
    Records_Measured = n(),
    Expansion = first(Species_weight) / first(Subsample_Total_W),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(Total_Weight_kg))

# View(top_influence_hauls)

fwrite(top_influence_hauls,
       here(dir, survey.path,
            "CPS.ATM.Survey.top_influence_hauls.minus.2007.csv"), 
       sep = ",")

# Load match summary 
Hauls2Fill.clean_sf.f.summary <-
  fread(here(dir, survey.path,
       "ATM.Survey.estimated.specimen.weight-lenComps.csv")
  )

Hauls2Fill.clean_sf.f.summary
# None of the top influenced hauls were estimated

#-----------------------------
# Check that for every haul, the sum of the 
# Scaled_Biomass_Contribution is equal to the Species_weight
test.total.bios <- final_production_data |>
  group_by(keys, Species_weight) |>
  summarise(TotScaleBio = 
    sum(Scaled_Biomass_Contribution),
    .groups = "keep"
    ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(TotalBioDiff = Species_weight - TotScaleBio) |>
  mutate(TotalBioDiff = round(TotalBioDiff, digits = 3)
         )
    

unique(test.total.bios$TotalBioDiff)
# [1] 0.000

#---------------------------------------------------------------
# Fourth, create plot showing the the biological weight per length
#---------------------------------------------------------------

# Isolate hauls where length weight were estimated
borrowed.us.haul.comps <- fread(
  here(dir, survey.path,
       "ATM.Survey.estimated.specimen.weight-lenComps.csv"), 
  sep = ",")

# Plot individual estimated weights per haul by length
## Note this includes the pseudo values!
Hybrid.reweighting.w.correction <-
  ggplot(final_production_data |>
           filter(!keys %in% borrowed.us.haul.comps$keys), 
         aes(x = standard_length, 
             y = Bio_Weight_kg,
             color = keys)) + # Move color inside aes()
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + # Alpha helps see overlapping points
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") + # Hides the massive legend
  labs(title = "Validation of Conditional Weighting Based on Observed Length Bins: Sardinops sagax",
       x = "Standard Length (cm)",
       y = "Hybrid Estimation Individual Weight (kg)")

Hybrid.reweighting.w.correction

ggsave2(
  filename="Hybrid.reweighting.w.correction.plot.USA.jpeg",
  plot=Hybrid.reweighting.w.correction, device="jpeg", 
  path=here(dir, figure.path), dpi=1200, width = 29, 
            height=21, unit="cm", limitsize = FALSE)

#---------------------------------------------------------------
# Fifth, create plot showing the the expansion weight per length
# bin
#---------------------------------------------------------------

# Plot individual estimated weights per haul by length
scaled.reweighting.w.correction <-
  ggplot(final_production_data, 
         aes(x = keys, 
             y = Scaled_Biomass_Contribution,
             fill = as.factor(len.bin)
             )
         ) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", 
           position = "stack", 
           linewidth = 0.01) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", 
                       name = "Length Bin (cm)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Proportional Biomass Distribution by Hauls",
    subtitle = "Total Haul Weights Partitioned by Length Bins",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Expansion Biomass Est. (kg)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

scaled.reweighting.w.correction

ggsave2(filename="expansion_biomass_per.haul.plot.USA.jpeg",
        plot=scaled.reweighting.w.correction, device="jpeg", 
        path=here(dir, figure.path),
        dpi=1200, width = 29, height=21,  
        unit="cm", limitsize = FALSE)

```

```{r, sardine.presence}
Sardine.present <- final_production_data |>
  group_by(keys, geometry) |>
  mutate(time.step = paste(Year," - ", Month, sep="")
         ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  distinct()

# View(Sardine.present)

```

# Expand spatial temporal elements for hauls with Sardine

```{r, Absent.bin}

Others <- full.series.sf |> 
  filter(scientific_name != "Sardinops sagax") |>
  group_by(cruise, ship, haul, collection,
           equilibrium_time.pacific, geometry
           ) |>
  mutate(time.step = paste(Year," - ", Month, sep="")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-c(longitude, latitude, is_random_sample)) |>
  distinct() |>
  mutate(weight = 0,
         Species_weight = 0,
         len.bin = NA,
         W_theory = 0,
         Condition_Factor = NA,
         W_best_estimate = 0,
         Bio_Weight_kg = 0,
         Subsample_Total_W = 0,
         Haul_Total_Catch_W = 0,
         Bin_Subsample_W = 0,
         Bin_Prop = NA,
         Bin_Haul_Biomass = 0,
         Indiv_W_Scaled = 0,
         Scaled_Biomass_Contribution = 0,
         Expansion_Factor = NA
         ) |>
  distinct()

```

# Sum tables and simplify

Check for unique keys where no sardines were caught. These will be treated as true absent values.

```{r, view.absent.present.data.structure}

# Check that no weird stuff is happening (there shouldn't be)
!colnames(Sardine.present) %in% colnames(Others)
#  [1] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
# [12] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE
# [23] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
# [34] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
# [45] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE

names(Sardine.present)[c(20:22)]
# [1] "latitude"          "longitude"         "is_random_sample" 

# Remove unnecessary columns
Sardine.present <- Sardine.present[,-c(20:22)]

# Double check column names from other direction
!colnames(Others) %in% colnames(Sardine.present)
#  [1] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
# [12] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
# [23] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE
# [34] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE

# Filter out hauls that had Sardine catch. What is left
# will be considered "true" absence.
Absent <- Others |>
  filter(!keys %in% Sardine.present$keys)
# View(Absent)

```

# Complete table joins

From the structure it is necessary to change the len.bin3 equilibrium_time.pacifc to POSIXct.

```{r, join.tables}

# Formats match, join the two data frames.
PreAbs <- bind_rows(Sardine.present, Absent) |>
  # Create a data object
  mutate(date = as.Date(equilibrium_time.pacific))
# View(PreAbs)

unique(is.na(PreAbs))

fwrite(PreAbs |> st_drop_geometry(), 
       here(dir, survey.path,
            "CPS.ATM.Survey.final.dat.csv"), sep = ";")

```

# Cluster hauls by date and sun event

This step is mainly for the summary table. 

## First find the corresponding sunrise and sunset times

This should be done by data, lat, and lon.

```{r, sunrise.table}

# 1. Turn back on s2 processing
sf_use_s2(TRUE)

# Find the center of the polygon layers to use for joins
PreAbs2 <- PreAbs |>
  mutate(
    lat = st_coordinates(st_centroid(geometry))[,2],
    lon = st_coordinates(st_centroid(geometry))[,1]
  )

# Use unique combinations from your data
suntimes <- PreAbs2 |>
  transmute(
    lat = lat,
    lon = lon,
    date = date
  ) |>
  distinct() |>
  st_drop_geometry()

dim(suntimes)
# [1] 2110  3

# Plan parallel execution (adjust workers if needed)
plan(multisession)

# Apply get_sun_times function in parallel.
## Note that get_sun_times must in wgs84 
sun_times <- future_pmap_dfr(suntimes, get_sun_times)

# Check that tz is correct
head(sun_times$sunrise_pacific)
head(sun_times$sunset_pacific)

#---------------------------------------------------------------
# Save (optional) : Note that the tz value is not stored and 
# needs specified manually each time you load data with a POSIXct 
# structure.
#---------------------------------------------------------------

# Where to save output:
## sun_times.dir <- here(getwd(), "Data", "Sun_times")

# Save as CSV:
## fwrite(sun_times, file = paste(sun_times.dir, "/sunrise_sunset_times.csv", sep=""), sep = ",")

```

## Join set set table with data for clusters

Note that you the code above returns an IDate column for date and needs converted to standard date.

```{r, join.sunrise.set.and.dat}

# Check reference system
st_crs(PreAbs2)

dim(PreAbs2)
# 1] 21347  48

# Check output
head(sun_times$sunrise_pacific)
head(sun_times$sunset_pacific)

dim(sun_times)
# [1] 2110   5

# Add sun_times to original data set
area.transects <- inner_join(PreAbs2, sun_times, 
                             join_by("date", "lat", "lon")) |>
  st_transform(crs = aea_custom)
# View(area.transects)  

dim(area.transects)
# [1] 21606    50

# Double check values
unique(is.na(area.transects))

```

## Create id for potential future work 

Determine whether the haul was taken during the day or night. 

```{r, join.sunrise.set.and.dat}

# Filter hauls that are taken before 
# sunset time that are after sunrise time
area.transects.d <- area.transects |>
  group_by(date) |>
  filter(equilibrium_time.pacific >= sunrise_pacific) |>
  mutate(cluster.grp = "day Trawl") |>
  ungroup()

# Filter hauls that are taken before 
# sunrise time that are after sunset time
area.transects.n <- area.transects |>
  group_by(date) |>
  filter(equilibrium_time.pacific < sunrise_pacific |
           equilibrium_time.pacific >= sunset_pacific) |>
  mutate(cluster.grp = "night Trawl") |>
  ungroup()

# Join spatial objects and convert DateTime values to character 
# string (ESIRI does not work with DateTime)
area.transects.final <- bind_rows(area.transects.d, 
                              area.transects.n) |>
  mutate(haulback_time.pacific =
           as.character(haulback_time.pacific),
         equilibrium_time.pacific = 
           as.character(equilibrium_time.pacific),
         sunrise_pacific = as.character(sunrise_pacific),
         sunset_pacific = as.character(sunset_pacific))

dim(area.transects.final)
# [1] 21606  49

# View(area.transects.final)

fwrite(area.transects.final |> st_drop_geometry(), 
       here(dir, "Data", "area.transects.pre-step.csv"),
       sep = ",")

```

```{r, join.sunrise.set.and.dat}

# sunset time that are after sunrise time

  group_by(date) |>
  filter(equilibrium_time.pacific >= sunrise_pacific) |>
  mutate(cluster.grp = "day Trawl") |>
  ungroup()
  
# Filter hauls that are taken before 
# sunrise time that are after sunset time
area.transects.n <- area.transects |>
  group_by(date) |>
  filter(equilibrium_time.pacific < sunrise_pacific |
           equilibrium_time.pacific >= sunset_pacific) |>
  mutate(cluster.grp = "night Trawl") |>
  ungroup()
  
# Join spatial objects and convert DateTime values to character 
# string (ESIRI does not work with DateTime)
area.transects.final <- bind_rows(area.transects.d, 
                              area.transects.n) |>
  mutate(haulback_time.pacific =
           as.character(haulback_time.pacific),

       here(dir, "Data", "area.transects.pre-step.csv"),
       sep = ",")

area.transects.final <- area.transects.final |>
  mutate(FID = row_number())

# Note data will be in wgs84
area.transects.final.sf <- 
  make_transect_sf(area.transects.final, crs = 4326) 

# Define Season
sort(unique(area.transects.final.sf$Month))
# [1]  3  4  5  6  7  8  9 10 11

area.transects.final.sf <- area.transects.final.sf |>
  mutate(Season = case_when(
    month(date) %in% c(3:5) ~ "Spring",
    month(date) %in% c(6:9) ~ "Summer",
    month(date) %in% c(10:11) ~ "Fall")
  )

```

# Calculate distance between start and stop of haul

```{r, start.stop.dist}

area.transects.final.cln <- area.transects.final.sf |>
# Define coordinate pairs
  group_by(keys) |>
  mutate(
    start.coords = purrr::pmap(
      list(start_longitude, start_latitude),
      ~ st_point(c(..1, ..2))
    ) |>
      st_sfc(crs = 4326),

    end.coords = purrr::pmap(
      list(stop_longitude, stop_latitude),
      ~ st_point(c(..1, ..2))
    ) |>
      st_sfc(crs = 4326)
  ) |>
  ungroup()  

area.transects.final.cln <- area.transects.final.cln |>
  group_by(keys) |>
  # Calculate distance travelled
  mutate(dist.trvl = geosphere::distVincentyEllipsoid(
    p1=st_coordinates(start.coords),
    p2=st_coordinates(end.coords),
    a=6378137,
    b=6356752.3142,
    f=1/298.257223563)) |>
  ungroup() 

head(area.transects.final.cln$dist.trvl)

```

# Check for entries where start and stop are the same

```{r,start.stop.equal}

# How many observations have the same start and stop
dropped.dat <- area.transects.final.cln |> 
  mutate(dist.trvl.m = as.numeric(dist.trvl)) |>
  filter(dist.trvl == 0)

length(unique(dropped.dat$keys))
# [1] 9

# Filter out observations with same start and stop
area.transects.final.cln2 <- area.transects.final.cln |> 
  mutate(dist.trvl.m = as.numeric(dist.trvl)) |>
  filter(dist.trvl.m != 0)  |>
  select(-dist.trvl)

# Check if there is a consistent haul distance -1 year
test.2006 <- area.transects.final.cln2 |>
  filter(Year == 2006 & 
           substr(cruise, nchar(cruise)-1, nchar(cruise)) == "04")
range(test.2006$dist.trvl.m)
# [1] 2910.914 4024.486

# Check if there is a consistent haul distance +1 year
test.2008 <- area.transects.final.cln2 |>
  filter(Year == 2008 & 
           substr(cruise, nchar(cruise)-1, nchar(cruise)) == "04")
range(test.2008$dist.trvl.m)
# [1] 2809.329 7815.978

```

## For 2003-2005

1) Lo, N.C.H., Macewicz, B.J., Griffith, D.A. 2011. BULLETIN OF MARINE SCIENCE. 87(3):395–412. http://dx.doi.org/10.5343/bms.2010.1077

2) Emmett RL, Brodeur RD, Miller TW, Pool S, Bentley PJ, Krutzikowsky GK, Mccrae J. 2005. 
Pacific sardine (Sardinops sagax) abundance, distribution, and ecological relationships in the Pacific northwest. calif coop oceanic invest rep. 46:122–143.

```{r, sweep.area.2003-2005}

area.transects.final.2003.2005 <- 
  area.transects.final.cln3 |>
  filter(Year %in% c(2003:2005)) |>
  # Nordic264 rope, 30 min, 4 knots ~360m2 (20m * 18m)
  mutate(area.op.m2 = 20*18) |>
  mutate(sweep.m3 = area.op.m2*dist.trvl.m) |>
  distinct() |>
  # Calculate density for total haul
  mutate(
    Haul.kg.m3 = Species_weight/sweep.m3,
    Haul.g.m3 = Species_weight*1000/sweep.m3
    ) |>
  distinct() |>
  # Calculate density per length bin
  group_by(keys, len.bin) |>
  # Calculate density for total haul
  mutate(
    LenBin.kg.m3 = Bin_Haul_Biomass/sweep.m3,
    LenBin.g.m3 = Bin_Haul_Biomass*1000/sweep.m3) |>
  distinct() |>
  ungroup()

# View(area.transects.final.2003.2005)
```

```{r, sweep.area.2015-2020}

area.transects.final.2015.2020 <- 
  area.transects.final.cln3 |>
  filter(Year %in% c(2015:2020)) |>
  # Nordic264 rope, 30-45min, 3.5-5 knots ~300m2 (15m * 20m) 
  mutate(area.op.m2 = 15*20) |>
  mutate(sweep.m3 = area.op.m2*dist.trvl.m) |>
  distinct() |>
  # Calculate density for total haul
  mutate(
    Haul.kg.m3 = Species_weight/sweep.m3,
    Haul.g.m3 = Species_weight*1000/sweep.m3
    ) |>
  distinct() |>
  # Calculate density per length bin
  group_by(keys, len.bin) |>
  # Calculate density for total haul
  mutate(
    LenBin.kg.m3 = Bin_Haul_Biomass/sweep.m3,
    LenBin.g.m3 = Bin_Haul_Biomass*1000/sweep.m3) |>
  distinct() |>
  ungroup()

# View(area.transects.final.2015.2020)

fwrite(
  area.transects.final.2015.2020, 
  here(
    dir, "Data", "ATM CPS Survey", "area.transects.final.2015.2020.csv"), 
  sep = ",")

test.range4 <- area.transects.final.2015.2020 |>
  filter(!Month %in% c(10:11))

range(test.range4$start_latitude)
# [1] 32.1748 54.3102

range(test.range4$stop_latitude)
# [1] 32.1355 54.2875

```
